item: dayz-rag MCP server (server.py, voyage_common.py, README, tests)
reason: Mostly solid. The 75 MCP tests pass (py -m pytest -q .claude/mcp/dayz-rag). In the full requested suite, 3 of 4528 tests fail, all outside this server. All three tools carry readOnlyHint, and openWorldHint is set correctly: true for the search tool, false for the two local tools. Tool descriptions are clear. Errors raise and reach the client with isError=true, and a test runs this through the MCP layer. Retries, the cache, rebuild detection, the drive guard and worker-thread offload are all tested. The README matches the code. One concrete defect confirmed on P:: get_dayz_file only applies its 200 KB limit when neither line_start nor line_end is given. So get_dayz_file('P:\DZ\sounds\hpp\config.cpp', line_start=1) returned 10,239,845 characters (523,051 lines), and the size error only appeared when no range was passed. An agent that passes just a start line on a big config.cpp or mapgroupcluster.xml gets megabytes back and floods its context. A second, latent mismatch: _slice_lines uses str.splitlines(), but the indexer's _split_lines deliberately splits on '\n' only, because splitlines also breaks at \f, \v, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and \u2028. For 'a\fb\nc', the server returns 'b' as line 2 where the indexer counts 'c'. A scan of P:\scripts and P:\DZ found no such characters today, so this only bites on future or modded files. Minor issues: _read_manifest does not catch UnicodeDecodeError, so a manifest that is not valid UTF-8 errors without the rebuild hint. The search docstring lists stale_reason as always present, but it only appears on stale hits.

Almost everything checks out. All 36 scripts\dayz rows, the 6 setup rows and the 3 dev rows match a real .bat file, and every wrapper's target script exists. Every flag or subcommand used in an example is in the target's --help: --author, --source, --piece, vest, gate build, --stdin, --server, --mod, check, --merge, --version, --mission, --full, --grep, --keep-server, --remove, --status, --agents. The Python fallback note is accurate: stop-test.bat has no fallback, and dayz-search.bat is the only scripts\dayz wrapper without the [FAIL] line. The paid-API notes are accurate: Voyage, the free-tier prompt in index.py, TypeSafe Jev only when the key is set, and evals.bat costing tokens. The panel install line matches .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. The clean-repo and clean-workspace rows match their code: .git folders are skipped, and --include-server removes all of .server. Its tests in scripts/dev/test_repo_integrity.py pass. The full run (py -m pytest -q .claude scripts/dev hooks) gave 3 failed and 4525 passed; none of the 3 failures involves this README. Problems a user would hit: (1) The sync-skills.bat row says 'Claude Code with --agents claude'. Running `sync-skills.bat --agents claude` links only Claude Code and drops Codex and Gemini, because --agents replaces the default list in sync.py. A user who wants all three gets one. (2) The clean-workspace.bat row says it deletes the deployed P:\Mods\@<ModName>\ copies. clean.py removes one only when its ownership marker matches, so a hand-copied or older deploy stays and the user does not know why. (3) The Python-missing message only covers scripts\dayz. The setup wrappers, which a new user runs first (for example preflight.bat), have no [FAIL] guard. Without Python the user gets a bare 'py is not recognized' error, and the README says nothing about that case. (4) The ask.bat note says every question goes to Voyage. Without VOYAGE_API_KEY, ask.py falls back to grep on its own, which the README does not say.

All 49 tests in hooks/test_scope_guard.py pass (8.8 seconds), and every test drives the hook through stdin. The output is correct PreToolUse JSON: hookSpecificOutput holds hookEventName PreToolUse, permissionDecision deny and a reason Claude can act on. Bad stdin, a corrupt state file and errors inside the hook all exit 0 with no output, so the hook never blocks on its own bug. The project wiring in .claude/settings.json and the plugin wiring in hooks/hooks.json both match Edit|Write|MultiEdit and have a 10-second timeout. The docstring matches the code. I also probed paths by hand. These were blocked: short 8.3 names (OTHERM~1, WORKSP~1, including a file that does not exist yet), alternate data streams (a.c:ads), the ::$INDEX_ALLOCATION directory form, non-ASCII file names, and the P:\Other and P:\Mods\@Other forms. Two gaps remain that a user would actually hit. First, a sibling mod that is still being created is not guarded: while scoped to MyVest, Claude can write workspace/BrandNew/scripts/3_Game/x.c, mod.cpp and the rest of a new mod, as long as config.cpp or $PBOPREFIX$ is written last. Only the marker write at the folder root is caught. Second, the hook matches Edit, Write and MultiEdit only, so a Bash or PowerShell write into another mod's folder (redirect, cp, sed -i, Set-Content) passes. The docstring states this second gap. There are also small test gaps: no test covers the 8.3 short-name claim, a state file whose JSON is valid but not an object, or a missing preflight.py or game install on the !Workshop path.

All 18 tests pass in 0.16s, and the full suite (1417 tests) passes. Each scan has a test that feeds it a synthetic bad case, so the checks for modded-member clashes, cross-file names and layers, duplicate RPC handlers and unused fields are each shown to fail when they should. Every P: citation holds when opened: staminahandler.c:335-338 sets stamina from GetStaminaMax, cfggameplayhandler.c:217-220 is GetStaminaMax, playerbase.c:4607-4610 is the EOnFrame client and IsControlledPlayer guard, dayzgame.c:2848 and :2914-2917 forward OnKeyPress to the mission, and uimanager.c:59 is GetMenu. Three concrete defects remain. First, _method_body counts braces in the raw source without removing strings or comments, so a method that later gains a line such as Print("}") or a comment ending in '}' is cut short. The hover, hotkey, stamina and EOnFrame tests then fail even though the code is correct, or pass without having looked at it. Second, _cross_file_problems searches code that still contains string literals, so a Print("MyMod_Item") in another file counts as a use and wrongly demands a note naming the declaring file. Third, the _FUNC negative lookahead skips any line that starts with 'static', so two files that each declare the same file-scope static function would not be reported as a duplicate.

I opened every P: citation in the file (canteen.c:1, playerbase.c:359-364, 2042, 3007, 3129, 6170, 6733, 8121, 7353-7361, 7408-7421, entityai.c:227, 2843-2850, 3064, eagents.c:9, poisoning.c:32, staminahandler.c:335-338 and 1081, cfggameplayhandler.c:217-220, cfggameplaydatajson.c:135, constants.c:749, playerstatspco.c:340, playerconstants.c:45, missionserver.c:781, missiongameplay.c:230, inventory.c:121-128, gameplay.c:4-11, presethandlers.c:179, bloodregen.c:14, and characters config.cpp:122, 378-382, 412-414). Two concrete defects remain. (1) The IS_EXHAUSTED check in MyMod_UpdateSyncFlags (line 98) compares raw stamina against 10. The same file explains that raw stamina runs from 0 to the server's staminaMax setting and adds MyMod_GetStaminaPct for that reason, but this check does not use it. On a server with staminaMax set to 1000, the flag only turns on at 1 percent stamina. (2) OnScheduledTick (lines 140-150) does its work after super returns. Vanilla's early return for players who are not selected or not alive (playerbase.c:3009-3010) only exits the super call, so the mod still decays reputation and rebuilds sync flags for dead and not-yet-selected players. Two smaller points: the null check in MyMod_GetStaminaPct (line 243) can never fire, because vanilla Init creates the stamina handler (playerbase.c:414). OnStoreLoad also does not reject a save whose version is newer than MYMOD_PLAYER_STORE_VERSION, which happens after a mod downgrade.

Line 52 says that to copy autokey on purpose you call bpy_extras.anim_utils.AutoKeying.key_transformation(context, target). In bpy_extras.anim_utils, key_transformation takes (target, options) and keys without checking the user's autokey setting. The method that follows autokey is autokey_transformation(context, target). A script written from line 52 would pass the wrong arguments or key the wrong thing. To reach A+, change line 52 to name AutoKeying.autokey_transformation(context, target), or describe key_transformation(target, options) correctly.

It sets parent.location = (5, 5, 5) through the data API and then reads parent.matrix_world.inverted() on the next line, claiming the child goes back to (1, 0, 0). A bare transform write does not update matrix_world until the depsgraph is evaluated, so the inverse comes out as identity and the child stays at (6, 5, 5). To reach A+, add bpy.context.view_layer.update() in that snippet after parent.location is set and before matrix_parent_inverse is assigned (lines 89 to 92).

One concrete defect. skills/_shared/animation/blender-bpy-fcurve-modifiers.md:47 says the Cycles modifier's mode_before and mode_after default to NONE. That is the static RNA enum default only. Blender's fcm_cycles_new_data ('turn on cycles by default') sets both to Repeat (FCM_EXTRAPOLATE_CYCLIC), so fcurve.modifiers.new(type='CYCLES') loops in both directions straight away, and line 55 already relies on that. Fix: change '(`NONE` default, `REPEAT`, `REPEAT_OFFSET`, `MIRROR`)' to '(`NONE`, `REPEAT`, `REPEAT_OFFSET`, `MIRROR`; `modifiers.new()` sets both to `REPEAT`, so set `mode_before = 'NONE'` when only the end should loop)'. The pack's lead recipe is wrong for DayZ. skills/_shared/ui/localization.md:5 to :28 tells the reader to put a stringtable.xml (the Arma 3 Project/Package/Key format) at the addon root, and :3 calls it one of 'the two stringtable formats'. One concrete defect: dust-agents-and-protection.md:29, :33 and :69 present the dose as a fractional float (base dose 1.0 per second, times intensity, then (1 - protection) * m_TransferabilityIn * dose). On P: the dose passes through `int dose_size` in TransmitAgentsEx (plugintransmissionagents.c:306) and in CalculateAgentsToTransmit (:614), so the fractional per-tick dose (intensity * 1.0 * deltaT on a 1 s tick, DEFAULT_TICK_TIME_ACTIVE_SHORT = 1 at modifiersmanager.c:28) is truncated to a whole number before protection and transferability apply. A partial-intensity storm therefore passes 0 agents on most ticks. This is the same int truncation that heat-stroke.md relies on for the water drain constants. Fix: add a sentence after line 29 that the dose is converted to int at plugintransmissionagents.c:306 and :614, so only whole agents per tick get through and an intensity times deltaT below 1 transmits nothing. item: dayz-rag MCP server (server.py, voyage_common.py, README, tests)
reason: The server code is sound and its tests pass: python -m pytest -q .claude/mcp/dayz-rag gave 79 passed. All three tools carry readOnlyHint, search_dayz_source carries openWorldHint true and the two local tools set it false, errors are raised so FastMCP returns isError results (a test checks this over a real client), VALID_FILE_TYPES matches EXT_TYPE_MAP in skills/dayz-search-index/index.py lines 696-707, the manifest fields the server reads (indexed_at, embed_model) and the file_hashes.json keys (str(path)) match what index.py writes at lines 1133 and 1236-1256, and every voyageai.error class named in voyage_common.py TRANSIENT_ERROR_NAMES exists in the installed voyageai. One concrete defect, a README that does not match the repository's wiring: .claude/mcp/dayz-rag/README.md line 33 says that in a clone `.mcp.json` at the repo root declares the server and that `.claude/settings.json` sets "enabledMcpjsonServers": ["dayz-rag"], but the committed .mcp.json is {"mcpServers": {}} and .claude/settings.json has no enabledMcpjsonServers key; a clone gets the server only through the agentic-z plugin enabled in .claude/settings.json (enabledPlugins, line 108-109) and registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json. Line 11 repeats the error by saying a clone exposes the tools as mcp__dayz-rag__<tool> via .mcp.json. Fix: rewrite README line 33 to say the server is registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json and a clone loads it through the agentic-z plugin that .claude/settings.json enables, so .mcp.json declares no servers; and change line 11 to say the tools appear as mcp__plugin_agentic-z_dayz-rag__<tool> (mcp__dayz-rag__<tool> only if a user adds the server to .mcp.json themselves).

The server code is sound and well tested: python -m pytest -q .claude/mcp/dayz-testbridge ran 247 tests and all passed. The read-only tools (list_commands, session_status, logs_since) carry readOnlyHint and do not write. The tools that change state are not marked read-only. Failures raise and FastMCP returns them as error results. The plugin registration in .claude-plugin/plugin.json matches the README. On P:, centraleconomy.c:31 (ECE_NOPERSISTENCY_WORLD = 8388608) and :38 (ECE_PLACE_ON_SURFACE = 1060) hold. Several comments and docs do not match the code or the repository, and these are the concrete defects. (1) allowlist.py:28 cites ECE_ROTATIONFLAGS at centraleconomy.c:15, but line 15 is ECE_OBJECT_SPAWNER = 256 and ECE_ROTATIONFLAGS = 512 is on line 16. Fix: change ':15' to ':16'. (2) allowlist.py:139 cites 'feature-gaps.md, item 24', but no file named feature-gaps.md exists anywhere in the repository. Fix: point the comment at an existing file, such as skills/dayz-launch-test/references/test-bridge.md, or drop the citation. (3) README.md:24 says `peer` is needed 'only for ping, mark and vehicle_state', and the command tool docstring at server.py:224-225 says the same. But `exec` is also a both-peer command (allowlist.py:180), and bridge.py:125-126 refuses it without `peer`. Fix: add `exec` to both lists. (4) The module docstring at server.py:3-12 lists the server's tools but leaves out session_restart and session_restart_client, which server.py:207-219 registers. Fix: add both to that list. (5) README.md:36 promises 'at most 50 spawns a session', and allowlist.py:35 and bridge.py:136 say the same. But session.restart resets the counter to 0 (session.py:323) while keeping the same session and token, so a session that has been restarted allows more than 50 spawns. Fix: say the limit is 50 spawns per server start, reset by session_restart.

The panel works and is well tested: claude plugin test mods/agentic-z-panel ran 40 tests with 40 passing, claude plugin validate passed, and the panel check in scripts/dev/test_repo_integrity.py (21 tests) passed. Every skill script the buttons name exists, and the arguments the panel passes match each script's parser (ask.py accepts --top-k up to 25 and --excerpt-lines up to 300 and exits 1 when it finds nothing, health.py inserts the show subcommand, add_server.py takes the instance as a positional argument, logwatch.py takes --since, --duration and --mod, and the Workbench launcher takes --mod). The marketplace lists the panel at 0.8.1, matching plugin.json. Three concrete text defects remain. First, mods/agentic-z-panel/README.md:17 says the buttons sit in cards named 'Build and check' and 'Test session', but register.tsx:621-713 draws cards titled Status, Start a project, Build and test, Tools and Ask vanilla DayZ; the fix is to change the list to 'Start a project, Build and test, Tools, Ask vanilla DayZ'. Second, mods/agentic-z-panel/hooks/register.tsx:28 tells the user on the Keys tab that VOYAGE_API_KEY is used by 'the Ask tab', but there is no Ask tab (the tabs are Panel, Answer and Keys, and the ask is a field on the Panel tab); the fix is to say 'the ask field', as README.md does. Third, mods/agentic-z-panel/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:4 lists the /dayz-ask field among the actions and then says 'these actions cost no model tokens', but an ask with evidence calls $.model.complete with Sonnet (register.tsx:256) to write the answer; the fix is to say the buttons cost no model tokens and the ask field uses a short model call to write its answer.

I read all eight files ($PREFIX$, config.cpp and the six script files) and found no concrete defect. The mod-related tests pass: python -m pytest -q on .claude/mcp/dayz-testbridge/test_mod_matches_allowlist.py and test_vanilla_calls.py gave 178 passed with P: mounted, so every engine name the mod calls is pinned to a declaring line on P:\scripts, and each peer's command switch and the AZB_Args and AZB_Command wire fields match allowlist.py and bridge.py. I opened the comment citations on P: and they hold: game.c:777 ExecuteEnforceScript, playerbase.c:5982 the console's ExecuteEnforceScript call, scriptconsoleenfscripttab.c:131 the #ifdef DEVELOPER guard, object.c:821-826 GetNetworkIDString joining high and low with no separator, game.c:356 GetObjectByNetworkId(low, high), game.c:218 RequestExit and chernarusplus.c:252 RequestExit(IDC_MAIN_QUIT), carscript.c:1713 OnBeforeEngineStart checking the operational requirements, hatchback_02.c:218-226 CrewCanGetThrough refusing seat 0 with the door closed, actioncardoorsoutside.c:104 SetAnimationPhase, weather.c:203 wind magnitude in m/s, dayzplayerimplementmeleecombat.c:674 the layer mask, dayzphysics.c:101 the proxy parent, entityai.c:879 GetHierarchyRoot, human.c:10 ENABLED holding until DISABLED and human.c:259/262 the aim overrides, actiontargetscursor.c:658 GetActions, constants.c:184 and :192 MENU_INGAME and MENU_CHAT_INPUT, cctcursornoruincheck.c:38-43 measuring from the cursor hit, carscript.c:1041 OnInput and :1159-1199 the manual gear logic, missiongameplay.c:298 m_PauseQueued (a protected member, so the modded class can reset it), and dayzplayerimplement.c:3865 the developer server-walk override. The code's enum handling matches the allowlist choices (ui_open ingame, chat, close sent as widget; spawn_in_inventory hands, cargo, attachment; raycast modes; inventory_move destinations), sample_hz has a lower bound of 0.5 on the host so the drive interval cannot divide by zero, every script file is inside #ifdef DIAG_DEVELOPER as config.cpp states, the peer stays inactive without a 32-character -azBridge token, exec stays off without -azBridgeExec=1 and is documented as refused on DayZ Diag 1.30 (an accepted fact), and /dayz-release-pack does refuse a release naming AZ_TestBridge or an AZB_ class (release_pack.py:338-339) as config.cpp says.

The test suite passes (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-3d-viewer: 19 passed). The README commands, the exit-code table, the py3d fork gate (py3d 1.10.1 with IS_DAYZ_FORK in scripts/tools/py3d), the LOD kinds in classify_lod against py3d.classify_lod_resolution, the KNOWN-ISSUES entries (SWIZ never applied, proxies exported, 1100 reported as unknown) and the three.js 0.185.1 jsDelivr import map all match the code. Two concrete defects remain. First, scripts/tools/dayz-3d-viewer/dayz_3d_viewer/viewer_template.py:410 builds the embedded-mode texture with new T.Texture(img), whose flipY defaults to true, while the UVs it is given come from extract_lod_geometry (p3d_to_gltf.py:112), which already writes them in glTF orientation (1 - v); web mode loads the same UVs through GLTFLoader, which sets flipY to false. So every textured model renders vertically mirrored in one mode compared with the other, and the two modes the README presents as the same model cannot both be right. Fix: add tx.flipY=false; next to tx.needsUpdate=true at viewer_template.py:410 so the embedded viewer uses the same glTF UV convention as the .glb. Second, scripts/tools/dayz-3d-viewer/dayz_3d_viewer/paa_to_png.py:274 unpacks the PAA type with struct.unpack on handle.read(2) without checking its length, so paa-to-png on an empty or truncated file prints a raw struct.error traceback (reproduced with an empty .paa: Traceback ... struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 2 bytes, exit 1) instead of the one-line message the tool gives for other bad input; decode_mipmap at paa_to_png.py:339 likewise indexes self.mipmaps without a check and raises IndexError for a file with no mipmaps. Fix: in _parse, raise ViewerError('%s is not a PAA file (truncated header)') when fewer than 2 bytes are read, and have decode_mipmap call get_largest_mipmap() (or check the list) so an empty mipmap list raises the existing ViewerError('No mipmaps found in PAA file').

No concrete defect found. No concrete defect found. The tool's tests pass (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-layout-viewer/tests: 4 passed). I ran python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-model-preflight/tests from the repository root and all 74 tests passed with none skipped, so the jsonschema-based schema tests ran too. I read every source file against the README. The exit codes 0, 1 and 2 for PASS, FAIL and INVALID in __main__.py match the README table, and an unwritable --json target falls back to an INVALID result on stdout with PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT_UNWRITABLE and exit 2. The output is written to a temporary file and then replaced atomically, as documented. The contract loader in contract.py enforces exactly the documented rules: the source_model path is relative and must stay inside the contract directory, tolerance_m is a positive scalar or three positive values, selections are non-empty and unique, and the transform's last row must be [0,0,0,1]. The JSON schema in schemas/dayz-model-preflight-v1.schema.json agrees with the loader. In winding.py, a singular upper 3x3 is rejected, a positive determinant expects the vertex order preserved and a negative one expects it reversed, mixed winding is reported as a relation mismatch, and one-to-many lineage, a triangle mapped to a quad, duplicate mappings, uncovered faces and out-of-range faces are all rejected. Every finding code the code emits is in the README's stable code list, and the list has no extras. The library API in __init__.py exports PreflightError and run_preflight as the README shows, and run_preflight returns an INVALID result rather than raising. The fork check requires IS_DAYZ_FORK to be True and a version of at least 1.6.0. The bundled py3d at scripts/tools/py3d/py3d/__init__.py lines 54 and 55 declares version 1.10.1 and IS_DAYZ_FORK = True, and its severities are ERROR and WARN, which match the severity ordering in findings.py. The install path scripts/tools/py3d with its pyproject.toml exists. I found no concrete defect.

No concrete defect found. The tests pass: python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-navmesh-compare/tests gave 60 passed and 39 subtests passed. The four vanilla navmesh.nm files under P:\DZ\worlds (chernarusplus, enoch, sakhal, nasdara) start with TESM, carry file version 9 and tile version 12, hold 94 249, 65 536, 94 249 and 106 929 tiles (2 413 591 in total with the two custom pairs), have origin (0, 0, 0), and in every tile the uint32 at byte 8 of the 16-byte prefix equals the bytes to the next tile or the end of the file, exactly as navmesh_tiles.py and the README state. The seven tests in test_object_checks.py pass (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-object-checks: 7 passed), and the fake game checks every command against the real allowlist. First, scripts/tools/dayz-object-checks/object_checks.py:15 says the player 'must stay up there two seconds later', but the code at line 124 reads the height after a 0.5 second walk step (as skills/dayz-launch-test/references/test-bridge.md:101 also says); fix the docstring to 'after a half-second step'. Second, object_checks.py:20 and docs/tools.md:372 promise that every spawned object is removed with clear_spawns, but run_checks returns at line 62-63 without calling clear_spawns when the spawn succeeded but read back as a different type (for example a class name typed in different case), and any bridge error raised mid-run skips line 132 as well, leaving the object and the WoodenCrate control in a session the user started themselves; fix by wrapping the body after the spawn in try/finally that calls clear_spawns. Third, the positive control (line 98), the negative control rays (line 101) and the stand_on control drop (line 126) are all placed a fixed 3 m east or west of the object's centre, while docs/tools.md:365-368 present the tool for buildings with MyMod_Shed as the example; for any object more than about 6 m wide the 'empty spot' lies inside the object, so the negative control hits, controls_valid is false and collision and stand_on fail for a correct model, and the WoodenCrate spawns inside it; fix by placing the controls beyond the object's measured extent (for example from a ray or bounding size) or by stating in the docstring and docs/tools.md that the object must fit within 2.5 m of its centre.

All 49 tests pass (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-persistence-contracts, 49 passed). The README and docs/tools.md tables match the modules, every pack file the README names exists under skills/_shared/persistence/, the router matches the four questions and three rows of where-to-save.md, the checklist matches Hard stop 2, the stream model matches save-load-contract.md, and the sidecar save and orphan recovery sequence matches the eight steps and nine failure rows of sidecar-files.md. Three concrete defects remain, each confirmed by running the model. First, scripts/tools/dayz-persistence-contracts/persistence_cf.py:98 returns an empty successful load for every game version from 116 to 140 without reading the frame (a saved frame loaded with game_version=130 gives success, 0 bytes, no mods), but cf-modstorage.md:73 says the 141 cutoff only gates CF's entity list and that below 141 the reader goes on to read the frame; the fix is to drop the early return at line 98 (and rename FRAMEWORK_HEADER_GAME_VERSION to reflect the entity-list gate) so versions 116 to 140 read the framework version, mod count and blocks, and add a test for that range. Second, persistence_cf.py:103 to :115 accepts any framework version and any mod count (a frame with framework version 9 loads as success), while cf-modstorage.md:78 says a framework version above 5 or a mod count outside 0 to 256 makes the load return false; the fix is to return CFLoadResult(False, None, 0, framework_version) when framework_version > CF_FRAMEWORK_VERSION or mod_count > 256, with a test for each. Third, persistence_sidecar.py:163 decodes legacy bytes with errors='strict' outside a try block, so MigrationReader.read(b'LEGACY:\xff', ...) raises UnicodeDecodeError instead of classifying the input, contradicting migration-matrix.md:24 (a parse failure is not a legacy success) and the README's fail-closed claim; the fix is to catch UnicodeDecodeError there and return the reject_invalid result with state intact, plus a test.

The tests pass (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-vehicle-checks: 12 passed), and every bridge call in them is validated against the real allowlist. The script matches the bridge it drives: the allowlist's commands, peers and result fields (spawn, find_objects, raycast with parent_net_id, surface, vehicle_prepare with entry_pos, get_in with reason, player_state, drive, vehicle_state, get_out, delete), the get_in reason text built in AZB_ClientCommands.c:526-542 (possible=, through=, area_free=, reach=), MAX_DRIVE_S = 60 behind the --drive-s help text, and the session.py functions it calls. I also confirmed three vanilla facts on P:. GetObjectsAtPosition searches a circle (P:\scripts\3_game\global\game.c:918-923), so the site search at y=0 is valid. Transport.CrewCanGetThrough returns false (P:\scripts\3_game\vehicles\transport.c:727-730) and CarScript does not override it. Hatchback_02 has OnDebugSpawn (P:\scripts\4_world\entities\vehicles\inheritedcars\hatchback_02.c:393). Every reference file the fix texts name exists. One concrete defect is in the tool's own documentation. First, docs/tools.md:353 says the site check finds 'nothing in the 60 m lane ahead', but the code checks a 16 m lane (vehicle_checks.py:51 sets LANE_LENGTH_M = 16, and the script's docstring at line 11 also says 16 m). Second, docs/tools.md:353 says the checks run 'in the order of' vehicle-acceptance-checks.md, but the code runs conditioning before the solid rays and puts its own site check first, while that reference lists Solid before Conditioned. The script's docstring (lines 7-8) admits this change of order. Fix: reword docs/tools.md:353 to say the checks follow that reference, with the site check added first and conditioning moved before the solid rays.

I ran the tool's test suite from the repository root (python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/dayz-vehicle-proxy-contract/tests): 141 passed and 239 subtests passed, with no failures. The audit output files (report.json, summary.txt, lod-overview.json) match reporting.report_files. Audit refuses an existing --out directory and publishes the report tree atomically, so no partial report is left. Preview adds PNGs under preview/. Repair needs an absolute staging root outside addon_root, never writes into the source tree, and returns 1 when findings stay unresolved. The PBO byte-closure check compares source MLOD bytes with uncompressed entries, and compressed entries fail closed, which matches the README's pack-only warning. py3d is correctly described as not a declared dependency (pyproject.toml lists only numpy, scipy and matplotlib). The manifest loader rejects bad schemas with clear messages, and CfgConvert failures carry the command, exit code and output. I found no concrete defect. The only import that looks unused, load_obj_geometry in audit.py, is a deliberate test seam: test_declared_obj_geometry_is_parsed_from_accepted_snapshot_bytes patches it.

One concrete defect. scripts/tools/py3d/README.md:309 says a plain run of `python -m pytest -q scripts/tools/py3d` from the repository root gives 399 passing tests and 11 skipped, but running exactly that command gives 352 passed, 11 skipped; the fix is to change 399 to 352 in that sentence. I read render_check.mjs in full, confirmed the version handshake it relies on exists (skills/_shared/viewer_core.py line 612 emits window.__THREE_REVISION from the imported module's REVISION, and THREE_VERSION 0.185.1 at line 45 splits to the revision 185 the gate compares), confirmed docs/tools.md line 279 matches the command, and ran it with no puppeteer installed: it printed the 'Cannot load puppeteer. Set PUPPETEER_MODULE' message and exited 2 as the comment promises. The tool has no tests of its own. Two concrete defects. First, scripts/tools/viewer-gate/render_check.mjs lines 46 to 47 say both dependencies resolve from the environment and that a miss says exactly what to set instead of throwing a stack trace, but only the puppeteer miss is handled: when no Chrome is found, findChrome returns undefined and puppeteer.launch at line 91 throws an uncaught error (for example puppeteer-core with no executablePath, or puppeteer with no downloaded browser), so the user gets a stack trace and exit code 1, the same code the script uses for a failed check, with no JSON. Fix: wrap the puppeteer.launch call at line 91 in try/catch, print 'Cannot launch Chrome. Set PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH (or CHROME_PATH) to a Chrome or Chromium binary.' with the error, and exit 2. Second, the usage text printed at line 85 omits the --min-tri-draws option that the header usage at line 41 documents and line 83 parses. Fix: change line 85 to 'usage: render_check.mjs <html|url> [--png f] [--expected-three V] [--min-draws N] [--min-tri-draws N]'.
